help.intro: A scene of about two minutes in a small shop: Leon is looking for a present for his grandmother's eightieth birthday, the shop assistant shows him scarves, gloves and a book, and they settle on which one, what colour and whether it should be wrapped. The scene is invented. You hear what you have just learnt: verbs with two objects and their order (Ich schenke ihr einen Schal: person in the dative first, thing in the accusative; with two pronouns the accusative comes first: Ich zeige ihn Ihnen), and the question words welcher? dieser? (Welchen Schal nehmen Sie? Diesen hier). Listen once for the whole scene, then once for the choices: which present, which colour, what price.
help.tips[0].title: Wem? Was? Two objects in one sentence
help.tips[0].text: geben, schenken, zeigen, bringen, empfehlen, kaufen take a person (dative) and a thing (accusative). Order with nouns: person first, then thing: Ich schenke meiner Oma einen Schal. Ich zeige Ihnen die Handschuhe. If the thing is a pronoun, it comes first: Ich zeige sie Ihnen. Ich schenke ihn ihr. If only the person is a pronoun, it stays first: Ich schenke ihr einen Schal.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I give my grandma a scarf. I give her a scarf. I give it to her.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Can you show me the gloves? Of course, I will show them to you.
help.tips[0].check.why: The person is in the dative: die Schwester → meiner Schwester; the book is the accusative object.
help.tips[1].text: welcher asks which one, dieser answers this one; both take the endings of der/die/das: Welcher Schal? Dieser. Welche Farbe? Diese. Welches Buch? Dieses. Accusative masculine: Welchen Schal nehmen Sie? Diesen hier. Dative: Mit welcher Farbe? Mit dieser. Plural: Welche Handschuhe? Diese.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Which scarf will you take, the blue or the green one? This one here, the green one.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: What size is your grandma? These gloves are size seven.
help.tips[1].check.why: das Buch is neuter: welches Buch, dieses Buch.
help.remember[0]: Ich schenke ihr einen Schal (Dat. then Akk.); Ich schenke ihn ihr (two pronouns: Akk. first).
help.remember[1]: Welcher Schal? Dieser. Welchen Schal? Diesen. Welches Buch? Dieses.
help.exam: Short shop scenes in which someone chooses and buys a present are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: A scarf, gloves or a book, and in which colour? Listen to Leon choosing a present for his grandmother's eightieth birthday.
passageTranslation:
Shop assistant: Good day! Can I help you?
Leon: Yes, please. I am looking for a present for my grandma. She turns eighty on Sunday.
Shop assistant: Eighty, how lovely! What does your grandma like?
Leon: She goes for a walk every day, even in winter. And she reads a lot.
Shop assistant: Then I have two ideas. I will show them to you. Here are scarves made of wool, very warm. And here are gloves made of leather.
Leon: The scarves are nice. Which scarf do you recommend to me?
Shop assistant: This one here, the green one. Green suits older ladies. Or this blue one, it is a bit thinner.
Leon: I think I will give her the green one. What does it cost?
Shop assistant: Thirty-nine euros. And the gloves? What size is your grandma?
Leon: I do not know. Her hands are small.
Shop assistant: Then better no risk. A book perhaps? Which books does she read?
Leon: Crime novels. But she already has them all.
Shop assistant: Then I will give you a voucher for the bookshop next door. With that she buys herself a new crime novel.
Leon: Good idea. So the scarf and a voucher for twenty euros.
Shop assistant: Shall I wrap the scarf for you as a present?
Leon: Yes, please. With a bow. My grandma likes bows.
Shop assistant: Which paper? This red one or this gold one?
Leon: The gold one. Eighty is almost gold, after all.
Shop assistant: With pleasure. That is fifty-nine euros all together. And give your grandma my best wishes!
Leon: I will tell her. Thank you very much!
